title: Trump, Aliyev and Pashinyan agree on the Trump Route through Armenia at the White House
body:
On 8 August 2025 US President Donald Trump hosted Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev at the White House. The three agreed on a route from Azerbaijan through Armenia to Nakhchivan, named the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity, abbreviated TRIPP. None of the leaders explained how the route would function or who would oversee it. Trump said Armenia was creating an exclusive partnership with the United States to develop the corridor for up to 99 years, renewable, and that he expected significant infrastructure development by American companies.

Trump and Pashinyan both said the route would not affect Armenia's sovereignty. Trump also ended a decades-old restriction on US defence cooperation with Azerbaijan that had been in place since the early 1990s. OC Media noted that US Ambassador Tom Barrack had proposed in a 12 July briefing a hundred-year lease on 32 kilometres of road, a figure that differs from Trump's.

Before the summit Aliyev had said on 19 July that no operator, trader or lessee could be on Azerbaijani territory, and Pashinyan's spokesperson Nazeli Baghdasaryan had denied that Armenia agreed to a corridor solution. Azerbaijani officials had called the route the Zangezur corridor. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova suggested on 24 July that Washington was co-opting the talks.
